players.product: Contracted hydro, wind, solar and battery-storage power for corporate and hyperscaler buyers, plus Westinghouse nuclear fuel, services and AP1000 reactors

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F (fiscal 2025): approximately 90% of its 2026 proportionate generation is contracted, with a weighted-average remaining duration of 13 years (proportionate basis) with creditworthy counterparties. In North America it sells power mainly through long-term PPAs with government-owned entities or power authorities (including Ontario's Independent Electricity System Operator, Hydro-Québec and BC Hydro), load-serving utilities (such as Entergy Louisiana), Brookfield, and industrial and commercial power users (including Amazon, Microsoft and Google); these PPAs are generally structured on an offtaker basis without fixed or minimum volume commitments, most carry annual inflation-linked price escalation, and the North American portfolio has a weighted average remaining contract term of 13 years.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 90% of 2026 proportionate generation contracted; 13-year weighted-average remaining duration

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F: in the U.S. it is primarily focused on power markets in the northeast (New York, New England), the mid-Atlantic (including the PJM ISO and north SERC regions), California, the Midwest (including the MISO region) and Texas (ERCOT), which the company says benefit from competitive wholesale power markets, growing electricity demand and an increasing need for reliable and flexible generation; the company says it is also seeing increasing demand for decarbonization-as-a-service, which it expects to be a multi-billion opportunity over the next decade.

Brookfield Renewable's 20-F: its total power portfolio is approximately 47,200 MW of installed capacity (capacity 47,203 MW at the end of 2025 vs 46,211 MW at the end of 2024) with a global development pipeline of over 200 GW. The renewable portfolio at December 31, 2025: hydroelectric 8,496 MW (239 facilities), wind 16,753 MW, utility-scale solar 13,993 MW and distributed energy & storage 5,503 MW, a total of 44,745 MW of renewable power. In the U.S., hydro capacity is concentrated in New York (74 facilities, 711 MW), Pennsylvania (four facilities, 747 MW) and New England (48 facilities, 700 MW); its U.S. hydroelectric reservoirs can collectively store approximately 2,500 GWh, and it holds a 50% joint-venture interest in a 666 MW hydroelectric pumped storage facility in Massachusetts. Total actual generation in 2025 was 116,010 GWh vs 80,842 GWh in 2024 (long-term average 123,028 GWh).
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 47,200 MW installed; pipeline over 200 GW; 44,745 MW renewable; 2025 generation 116,010 GWh

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F: capital expenditures, which mainly relate to the construction and maintenance of its renewable power generation fleet, were $6,587 million in 2025 vs $3,733 million in 2024 and $2,809 million in 2023. At December 31, 2025 it had $4,770 million of capital expenditure commitments outstanding (2024: $2,923 million), primarily contracted project costs for growth initiatives, of which $2,692 million is payable in less than one year, $1,982 million in two to five years and $96 million thereafter.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex $6,587 million (2024: $3,733 million); capex commitments $4,770 million (2024: $2,923 million)

quarterly_data.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F fiscal 2025 results: revenues $6,407 million vs $5,876 million in 2024; proportionate Adjusted EBITDA $2,698 million vs $2,408 million; Funds From Operations $1,334 million vs $1,217 million, or $2.01 per unit vs $1.83. Proportionate revenues by segment in 2025: hydroelectric $1,607 million, wind $596 million, utility-scale solar $469 million, distributed energy & storage $261 million and sustainable solutions $609 million (total $3,542 million vs $3,246 million in 2024). Proportionate FFO by segment in 2025: hydroelectric $607 million, wind $303 million, utility-scale solar $345 million, distributed energy & storage $453 million and sustainable solutions $161 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenues $6,407 million; FFO $1,334 million ($2.01 per unit)

connects_to.relationship: Hydro power supply under a 20-year contract (Safe Harbor hydro portfolio)

contracts.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F: in July 2025 Brookfield Renewable signed a Hydro Framework Agreement with Google (described by the company as first-of-its-kind) to deliver up to 3,000 MW of hydroelectric capacity in the U.S. by the end of 2032, including the first two contracts for 670 MW of capacity. The first contracted assets are hydroelectric facilities in Pennsylvania that Brookfield Renewable is relicensing; the two companies will initially focus on the mid-Atlantic and mid-continent electricity markets, with flexibility to expand into other U.S. regions.
contracts.units: up to 3,000 MW of U.S. hydroelectric capacity by the end of 2032; first two contracts for 670 MW

connects_to.relationship: New renewable energy capacity supply under a global renewable energy framework agreement

contracts.signal: Brookfield Renewable's 20-F: in May 2024 Brookfield Renewable and Microsoft signed a global renewable energy framework agreement that provides a pathway for Brookfield Renewable to deliver over 10.5 GW of new renewable energy capacity between 2026 and 2030 in the U.S. and Europe, with the potential to increase its scope to additional capacity in the U.S. and Europe and beyond to Asia-Pacific, India and Latin America; it supports Microsoft's goal of having 100% of its electricity consumption, 100% of the time, matched by zero carbon energy purchases by 2030.
contracts.units: over 10.5 GW of new renewable energy capacity, 2026 to 2030 (U.S. and Europe)
